rv.q: If you are in streaking distance, I can't imagine why you would not go.
That said, no studying (or looking up) is needed to keep pace with the teeming panoply of humanity that fills the stage in Writers Theatre’s magnificent production of Malloy’s Tony-winning musical.
It’s a joy to experience GREAT COMET end-to-end, and for musical theater lovers that want to hear a complicated score flawlessly performed, this is the ticket.
It is a profound conclusion to a show that deserves to be seen and will not soon be forgotten.
What appears to begin as a musical melodrama turns out to be a most imaginative, thought-provoking and highly entertaining theater production.
Altogether, it’s a compelling, cosmic adventure that just might be a once-in-a-lifetime event!
It’s a serious breath of fresh air for musical theatre as a genre.

Dave Malloy's electro-pop musical, a sung-through adaptation of a meaty hunk of Tolstoy's War & Peace, is directed and choreographed at Writers in its Chicago premiere with verve, wit and panache by Katie Spelman.
Katie Spelman’s magnificent production has Award-Winner written all over it.
Presented like a rave-adorned Fabergé egg, 'Great Comet' is an experience one must see to believe.
Still, as I have said, you simply won't find another show playing right now that is as stunningly well done as this one.

The stunning set design, lighting, and costumes were brought to life by the incredible work of three talented female designers, Courtney O'Neill, Raquel Adorno, and Yael Lubetzky, whose expertise truly elevated the overall theatrical experience.
A fine ensemble that truly makes this work a work of art.
Magnificently sung with grand costuming by Raquel Adorno and backed by inspired scenery design by Courtney O'Neill, 'Natasha…' looks and sounds like an award winner.
